A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LangHOPS and contain complete, readable main text, equations, figures, Tables 1–14, Appendix A and the checklist. The material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, ablations, robustness experiments and computational-cost measurements in Section 4 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v3 retains the original experimental outcomes in Section 4 and Appendix A, including the benchmark and ablation results in Tables 1–14.

M1.justification: The language-grounded hierarchy, PaliGemma 2 query refinement, segmentation decoders, training losses and feed-forward inference remain unchanged. Edits in Section 3 refine wording without changing the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Pascal-Part-116, PartImageNet and ADE20K evaluations, additional INS/PART training datasets, and appendix scenarios involving prompt permutations, synonyms and noisy hierarchies.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in corresponding experiments, including VLPart, PartGLEE and adapted PSALM for instance segmentation and the seven comparison methods in Table 3. The added citations introduce no evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The cross-dataset evaluations without finetuning, in-domain and zero-shot protocols, mAP/hIoU metrics, training configurations and appendix testing procedures are retained. Relocated ablation descriptions introduce no setting changes.

E4.justification: Both retain the object-part synergy, MLLM, hierarchy, training-stage, query-count and backbone ablations, plus failure cases and prompt/hierarchy robustness tests. The MLLM ablation discussion moves within Section 4.3 without changing its evidence.

E5.justification: Appendix A.2 and Table 8 retain the same three-random-seed evaluation and mean ± standard deviation reporting. The uncertainty reporting in Table 9 is also unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1–14 retain their numerical results and rankings. For example, Table 1 retains LangHOPS AP values of 26.7 for PPS-116+INS+PART to PartImageNet and 56.9 in-domain. Qualitative findings are also retained.

T1.justification: The problem definition and Equations 1–10 are mathematically unchanged, including query construction, losses and attention-score definition. Neither version contains formal theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same novelty, performance, generalization, scalability and object-part synergy claims. Their scientific scope is unchanged.

C2.justification: Both retain the same mechanism interpretations and limitations: computational expense, specialized-domain coverage, small or unseen parts, and annotation-style mismatches. Appendix explanations of robustness degradation are unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 3.6 retains the same implementation details, hyperparameters, four H200 GPUs and batch size 16. Appendix A.4 retains the resource measurements; the promised code release and its linked destination are unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to Mask R-CNN and Segment Everything Everywhere All at Once in the introduction's background discussion. The substantive related-work comparisons and LangHOPS positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized grammar and concision edits, reorders some Section 4.3 ablation discussion, expands affiliation wording and adds Section 6 acknowledging funding. The overall narrative and section organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: The author block is rearranged, Table 5 moves from page 9 to page 8 with shorter labels and caption, and surrounding text reflows. Figures 3–4 receive limited raster edits; no figures, tables or displayed analyses are added or removed.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves readability through grammatical corrections and tighter prose, adds background citations, and makes funding explicit in Section 6. These provide limited editorial and transparency benefits; the scientific evidence, reproducibility information and limitations remain unchanged.
